title: What are the angles when equal strips cross at forty degrees?
description: Two equal strips cut each other in half and cross at forty degrees, and the video finds every angle of the shape they make. Keeko then doubts that a crossing angle other than ninety degrees can give a rectangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: the crossing angle does not matter, because equal diagonals that cut each other in half always give four right angles. Watch for students who think the diagonals must cross at ninety degrees for the shape to be a rectangle.

source: Equal diagonals bisect each other at 40°. Find the angles of
video_script.why: The child sees that changing the crossing angle changes the triangles but not the corners, which prepares the general case for any crossing angle.
video_script.substitution: Find the angles at O, then the base angles of the two isosceles triangles, and add one of each at a corner.
video_script.anchor: quadrilateral ABCD whose equal diagonals AC and BD cross at O with 40 degrees between them
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says it cannot be a rectangle because the strips do not cross at 90 degrees; but the corners are 90 degrees whatever the crossing angle is.
video_script.payoff_line: All four angles are ninety degrees, so it is again a rectangle

final_answer.spoken: all four angles are ninety degrees, so it is again a rectangle

maths_rules: AC = BD and O is the midpoint of both, so OA = OB = OC = OD
angle AOB = angle COD = 40 degrees (vertically opposite); angle AOD = angle BOC = 180 - 40 = 140 degrees (linear pair)
triangle AOB with OA = OB: base angles add to 180 - 40 = 140, so each is 140 / 2 = 70 degrees
triangle AOD with OA = OD: base angles add to 180 - 140 = 40, so each is 40 / 2 = 20 degrees
SAS: triangle AOB is congruent to triangle COD and triangle AOD is congruent to triangle COB, so AB = CD and AD = CB, and the shape is a rectangle
video_script.design: One idea: the crossing angle does not change that the corners are right angles. Wrong idea: the strips must cross at ninety degrees. The figure with O and the forty degree angle stays on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks it cannot be a rectangle, because the strips do not cross at a right angle.

<bookmark mark='rule'/>Equal strips that cut each other in half always make a rectangle.
